reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. A single well-defined ring-enhancing lesion in the right parietal lobe with minimal surrounding edema. No additional lesions. No hydrocephalus or midline shift. No hemorrhage. Ventricles and extra-axial spaces otherwise normal.
reports.conclusion: Single ring-enhancing right parietal lesion with minimal edema.

reports.text: Specimen: brain, right parietal lesion, stereotactic needle biopsy. Sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells with an angiocentric pattern. Immunohistochemistry: CD20 positive, CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive; Ki-67 high. EBV (EBER) negative.
reports.conclusion: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, consistent with primary central nervous system lymphoma.

reports.text: Staging CT of the chest with IV contrast. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. No pleural or pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of lymphoma in the chest.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Staging CT. Postsurgical absence of the spleen. Liver, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys normal. No retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy. No masses.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of lymphoma in the abdomen or pelvis.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department, arrival 03/29/2024 19:20 by ambulance after a seizure at home.

HPI: 47F with SLE on chronic immunosuppression (hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg), status post splenectomy. Husband reports a week of worsening confusion and trouble with her vision, plus headaches; this evening a seizure at home, her first ever.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 bid, prednisone 10, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, KCl 20 mEq, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate. Allergy: sulfonamides.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable. Post-ictal at first, then slowly clearing but still disoriented to date. Left-sided weakness and poor coordination on the left. Fundi normal. Neck supple, no meningismus.

Workup: HIV screen negative. MRI brain with contrast: one well-circumscribed ring-enhancing lesion in the right parietal lobe, little edema. LP unremarkable.

MDM: new seizure and focal deficit from a solitary enhancing lesion in an immunosuppressed, asplenic host. Differential lymphoma vs infection vs other neoplasm. Levetiracetam loaded, then 500 mg twice daily. Neurosurgery and oncology consulted.

Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 03/29/2024, discharged 04/05/2024.

Principal diagnosis: primary CNS lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell type, right parietal lobe.
Secondary: new-onset seizure; SLE; hypertension; asplenia.

Hospital course: presented after a first seizure with a week of confusion, headache and visual disturbance; exam with left-sided weakness and incoordination. MRI showed a single ring-enhancing right parietal lesion with minimal edema. HIV negative. Lumbar puncture 3/30: WBC 2, protein 38, glucose 61, cytology negative. Stereotactic brain biopsy by neurosurgery 4/1 without complication; pathology diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, consistent with primary CNS lymphoma. Staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis showed no disease outside the CNS. Ophthalmology slit-lamp exam: no vitreous or retinal involvement. No further seizures on levetiracetam. Confusion improved; left-sided weakness improving with PT.

Discharge medications: NEW levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily. Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, potassium chloride 20 mEq, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate.
Allergies: sulfonamides.

Follow-up: neuro-oncology 4/12 to begin methotrexate-based chemotherapy. PCP within one week. No driving for six months after a seizure (Massachusetts law); patient and husband informed.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Call with hospital team
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Husband called the office - she had the brain biopsy yesterday, waiting on pathology. Spoke with the inpatient attending: preliminary read favors lymphoma, final pending; staging CTs tomorrow; oncology already involved. Gave them our direct line. Called husband back, offered support; will see her within a week of discharge.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with husband after admission 3/29-4/5. Seizure, solitary R parietal lesion; biopsy 4/1 = primary CNS lymphoma (DLBCL). Staging negative. Levetiracetam started. Discharge summary and path reviewed.

She is clearer. L hand still weaker, doing home exercises. No further seizures. Mild headache, Tylenol helps. Scared but ready to start treatment Friday. Husband driving her; she understands no driving 6 months.

Exam: alert, oriented x3, speech fluent. L grip 4/5, L finger-nose slightly clumsy. Biopsy site clean. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. PCNSL - oncology 4/12 to start high-dose MTX-based chemo. We'll coordinate; she can message any time.
2. Seizure - levetiracetam 500 bid, tolerating. No driving.
3. SLE - HCQ + pred 10 continue; rheum informed.
4. HTN - BP OK today. Watch K and Cr closely with MTX - oncology will draw.
5. Work: off for treatment, will complete leave forms.
Took time to talk through questions. RTC 2-3 months or as needed; telehealth fine during chemo.

documents.title: Neuro-oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology center, neuro-oncology. Seen 04/12/2024.

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Diallo is a 47-year-old with SLE on hydroxychloroquine and prednisone 10 mg, asplenia after a 2023 splenic rupture, and newly diagnosed primary CNS lymphoma (diffuse large B-cell) of the right parietal lobe, diagnosed by stereotactic biopsy 4/1/2024 after presenting with a seizure. Staging CT and slit-lamp exam showed no disease outside the brain; CSF cytology was negative.

She is recovering well from the admission and her left-sided weakness is improving.

Plan: induction with high-dose methotrexate and rituximab every two weeks for six cycles, starting today, as an inpatient for each methotrexate infusion with leucovorin rescue and level monitoring. If she responds, consolidation with high-dose cytarabine. We will reimage after induction. Continue levetiracetam. Hydroxychloroquine and prednisone continue; we have spoken with her rheumatologist. No live vaccines.

Allergies: sulfonamides.

Neuro-Oncology

Outside oncology center. Visit 08/12/2024.

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Diallo completed six cycles of high-dose methotrexate with rituximab on 7/19 with no significant toxicity apart from fatigue. She feels well and the left-sided weakness has resolved. No seizures.

She begins consolidation today with high-dose cytarabine, two cycles, finishing in September. We will repeat the brain MRI afterwards. Levetiracetam continues for now.

Neuro-Oncology

Outside oncology center. Visit 10/07/2024.

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Diallo finished consolidation cytarabine on 9/20. Her post-treatment MRI on 10/3 shows no enhancing disease: complete response.

Plan: surveillance MRI every three months for the first year, then every six months. Continue levetiracetam until the next scan, then we will discuss tapering. She may return to work when she feels ready; driving was permitted again from October given no seizures since March.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F annual exam.

The year: seizure 3/29 -> primary CNS lymphoma R parietal, biopsy 4/1; HD-MTX + rituximab x6 then cytarabine x2; MRI 10/3 complete response. Still on levetiracetam. Back at work part-time since November.

Feels 'about 80 percent.' Energy improving. Weight down a few kg from treatment. Mood: some worry before scans, sleeping OK. Hip unchanged. Lupus quiet.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 bid, prednisone 10, levetiracetam 500 bid, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, KCl 20 mEq, D3 2000 u, calcium carbonate 600 bid, acetaminophen prn.
Allergy: sulfonamides (severe rash).

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts no masses or nodes. Abdomen soft, healed scar. Pelvic normal, Pap/HPV obtained. Neuro: strength symmetric, gait antalgic (R hip) with cane. Skin clear.
PHQ-9 4.

Plan: labs. Pap/HPV today. Mammogram overdue (deferred during chemo) - order for early 2025. COVID booster after oncology OK. Next surveillance MRI January. HCQ eye exam due 2025.
RTC 3 mo.

Surveillance MRI on 1/9 shows no sign of recurrence. Ms. Diallo has had no seizures since March 2024 and has no residual lesion, so we are tapering levetiracetam: 250 mg twice daily for three weeks, then stop (last dose around 2/3). Next MRI in six months. She is cleared for the COVID vaccine.

events.reason: Fatigue and painful malar rash after prednisone course

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Visit 04/09/2025.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for managing her flare in March. Ms. Diallo, now 48, has had two weeks of mounting fatigue and a painful rash across both cheeks, which began a few days after she completed the 10-day prednisone course.

T 37.2 C, BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16. There is malar erythema with mild swelling. The rest of the exam is unchanged.

CBC: WBC 14.0 with 80% neutrophils and 10% lymphocytes, Hgb 12.2, platelets 220. ESR 50, CRP 4.5 mg/L.

Assessment: cutaneous lupus activity after the steroid taper, with leukocytosis. The leukocytosis is neutrophil-predominant in an asplenic patient who has just had extra prednisone; no sign of infection today.

Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily and prednisone 10 mg daily. Strict sun protection. Please repeat a CBC in about a month. I will see her in three months.

Allergies: sulfonamides.

Rheumatology
